Naomi / team —

I've reviewed Thermion's questionnaire and ran a quick pass on their DPA asks. High-level: we should be conservative on certain contract points but flexible on operational evidence. My suggested approach below — I'll attach a tracked-change redline for the Redwood DPA.

1) Processor role: Redwood accepts processor role; we will not take on controller obligations. We'll provide a subprocessor list that includes our cloud infra partner(s) and monitoring vendors. Proposed clawback: require Thermion to notify if they plan to instruct us to act as controller for specific processing activities.

2) Subprocessors: we will accept contractor/subprocessor flow-downs but will propose a narrower notice period (e.g., 10 business days) and allow us to temporarily block transfers for legal/regulatory reasons.

3) SCCs & Transfers: Redwood already executes SCCs with customers via the DPA. For customers wanting to rely on our hosted platform, we'll provide a TIA summary. If Thermion requires additional technical safeguards for US processing, we'll document them in the TIA addendum (TIA_summary.pdf).

4) Data retention & deletion: refuse open-ended retention exceptions; propose a maximum retention window in the Order Form or retention appendix.

5) Incident reporting & liability carveouts: keep standard vendor liability caps; push back on unlimited data liability language.

Next steps:
- I'm attaching my redline: Redwood_DPA_redline_karthik.docx (see Attachment).
- Soojin: please upload SOC 2 summary and an executed SCCs status report.
- Naomi/David: I'll plan to hand the redline off to Procurement thread once Soojin confirms the evidence set.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_redline_karthik.docx
